_serp_rotation_note: Index selects clusters (excluding aeo-sentinels) in portfolio order: for k in 0..2, cluster[(index+k) % n], query[floor(index/n) % len]. History: 0 = used-car-to-ebike / new-to-boston / family-logistics; 3 = year-round-weather / town-commuters / ebike-curious; 6 = employers-rto / schools-wellness / local-business-partners; 9-11 hand-advanced on 2026-09-14 to students-campus / drive-time-conversion / brand-navigational and the index parked at 12. On 2026-09-21 n was 13 (roams-trails shipped), so 12 wrapped to 0 on its own and the hand-correction that note predicted was NOT needed — the cycle restarted cleanly at used-car-to-ebike / new-to-boston / family-logistics. Index now 3. NOTE: if item 3 of 2026-09-21 ships, events-programs takes n from 13 to 14 and the cycle shifts again; the point is coverage over time, not a fixed cycle, so hand-correct and say so.

baselines._posthog_note: 71 organic sessions in the week starting 2026-09-14, against a trailing-4-week mean of 32.0 EXCLUDING it (+122%) and a 12-week mean of 30.3 (+134%). GSC agrees on direction (clicks 21 -> 34) but not magnitude, and the PostHog/GSC ratio moved from ~1.0-1.4 to 2.1. What argues it is real: the 71 spread across 25 landing pages with no single page dominating (home 13, /events/shift-your-summer 7, /shift-your-semester/berklee 5, then a tail of events/Roams/towns) — not a bot shape. Windows differ: PostHog is Monday-start (09-14 -> 09-20), GSC is Saturday-to-Friday (09-12 -> 09-18).

What is new is the SHAPE: one session each from three different engines, where every previous answer-engine referral came from one engine pointing at one contest-rules page and stopped when the contest ended. First weekly pulse after the Roams and Campus sections landed in llms.txt (79 -> 122 links); both facts are true and neither proves the other. Watch whether it persists.

resolved_notes.what: The routine had been reading `git diff main..branch` as a merge preview for three runs. It is not one: it compares two END STATES, so everything main gains after a branch is cut shows as a deletion the branch would supposedly make. That is where '241 files, -15,156 lines, would revert a week of work' came from on 2026-09-21. The real merge result for seo/2026-09-answer-schema was 2 files / +19 lines. seo/methodology.md had encoded the same misreading as doctrine since 2026-08-31 ('a drifted branch does not merely conflict, it silently reverts whatever landed after it was cut' — and, tellingly, 'only the diff stat gave it away').
resolved_notes.fix: Corrected the 'Keeping pending branches shippable' section of seo/methodology.md: what drift really costs (conflicts that grow with distance, a dishonest diff to approve, and a careless conflict resolution reintroducing pre-drift code), plus a new step 2 — check whether the branch is still the only copy of its change before rebasing it. Corrected the 2026-09-21 report in place with a marked correction block.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not quote `git diff main..branch --stat` as what a merge would do. Use `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only main <branch>` — non-zero exit means conflict and names the files; on clean exit, `git diff --stat main <printed tree>` is the true preview. And do not rebase a pending branch before checking whether its content already landed on main by another commit: `git branch --merged main` misses a re-implementation, which leaves the branch unmerged and looking live.

resolved_notes.what: The routine had been reading 40 rows of what is really a 128-row page table. pull-gsc.mjs asked Search Console for 500 page rows and persisted the top 40; at 2026-09-18 volumes those covered 85% of impressions and cut off at 22 impressions per page. Two reports' worth of conclusions were affected: /events (33 urls, 299 impressions, 7 clicks, 2.34% CTR — the best-converting class on the site) was filed as a rounding error for a month, and the 2026-09-14 watch item 'only 12 of 25 Roams are indexed' was a truncation artifact — 24 earn impressions.

resolved_notes.do_not: Do not assume a page is deindexed, cannibalised or failing because it is missing from the page table — check the table's ROW COUNT and its minimum impressions first. Do not compare page-level figures across 2026-09-18 without checking both weeks' cutoffs; earlier files cannot be corrected retroactively, so use a fixed cohort of pages present in both. And when raising a rowLimit asked of an API, check what is actually written to disk — the 2026-08-24 item raised the request to 500 and left the persist at 40, which is the bug that hid all this for a month.

resolved_notes.what: All four pending seo/ branches were dead. Three (llms-campus, roam-titles, roams-cluster) were already ancestors of main. The fourth, seo/2026-09-answer-schema, was NOT: Keith re-implemented its 62 lines directly as 049bc93, so the branch still carried a base from before the cream refresh and `git diff main..seo/2026-09-answer-schema` was 241 files / -15,156 lines. Merging it would have reverted a week of work.
resolved_notes.fix: Rebased nothing — a branch whose content has already shipped by another route should be deleted, not rebased. Reported all four as dead in the 2026-09-21 report and left deletion to Keith.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not rebase a pending branch without first checking whether its content already landed on main by another commit. `git branch --merged main` catches three of these four; the fourth needs an actual content check (grep the change on main), because a re-implementation leaves the branch unmerged and looking live. The methodology's 'rebase every pending branch' step assumes the branch is still the only copy of its change — verify that assumption first.

resolved_notes.what: Roam corrections: roams.distance_miles is a TRIGGER-COMPUTED sum of roam_legs.distance_miles (Shift 00282/00283) — setting it directly is not durable. Leg distances are measured along route_geometry by polyline_distance_miles(). Three trail maps (mcrt-sudhud, manhan, battle-road) were short because 00434 OSM lines ended before a required stop; legs past the end read 0.00 until the safe-route selector patched them with straight lines on 2026-05-20. resolved_notes.fix: Six Shift migrations (00918, 00919, 00920, 00922, 00923, 00924) applied with `supabase db push --yes` from the Shift repo, each pre-flighted (jsonb_typeof, md5, live checkpoints, dry-run of the leg recompute) and verified after. resolved_notes.do_not: Do not trust repo migrations for CURRENT roam data — read live rows (checkpoints moved in prod). Do not push two migrations at once when working one-at-a-time: `db push` applies every pending file. Check `ls supabase/migrations | tail` right before each push: another session took 00921 mid-run and the CLI recorded their number while my body applied unrecorded. Do not write `%%` in PL/pgSQL RAISE strings (the audit's first 00921 attempt failed on exactly that). Never use /admin/roams for these edits (it nulls route_geometry on save).

resolved_notes.what: Main moved twice mid-run (c1338ee, then 25d4151) from another session that also held uncommitted work in the shared working tree. Branch diffs quoted before that looked clean; afterwards the same branches showed 10-11 files and would have reverted the nearby/shuttle work. git checkout refused because of the live edits, so the methodology's rebase step could not be performed in the normal way.
resolved_notes.fix: Rebased all four seo/ branches in a throwaway `git worktree` under the scratchpad, force-pushed each with --force-with-lease, then removed the worktree. The other session's uncommitted edits were never stashed, checked out, or touched.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not stash or check out over another session's uncommitted work to satisfy the rebase step, and do not skip the step and quote a stale diff. Use a scratch worktree. Also: re-check `git log main` LATE in the run, not only at the start — main moving mid-run is normal on active days, and a diff verified at the top of the run may be wrong by the time the email goes out.

resolved_notes.what: Email 401 on the first attempts. Two different secrets share the name CRON_SECRET: gsi-website/.env.local holds the Vercel cron secret guarding this repo's /api/cron/* routes, while the Supabase edge functions use a separate deployed CRON_SECRET. The Shift project injects the Supabase-side value via an env block in its .claude/settings.local.json, which is why sentry-triage and plg-review (both run from the Shift directory) always worked. gsi-website had no env block, so $CRON_SECRET was empty here.
resolved_notes.fix: Added a matching env block to gsi-website/.claude/settings.local.json (gitignored). Verified: HTTP 200, sent to keith@gogreenstreets.org.
resolved_notes.do_not: Do not overwrite CRON_SECRET in .env.local to 'fix' this — that value is correct and in use by six Vercel cron routes.

declined.title: Commute Advisor FAQ: 'the most durable way' instead of 'the most sustainable way'
declined.reason: Keith: "We don't have a rule about 'never' using the word 'sustainable,' we just try to lead with practical benefits to active transportation." The sentence stays as written.
declined.do_not_repropose: Do NOT propose removing or swapping the word 'sustainable' from GSI copy again — not in page text, not in structured data, not in llms.txt. The guardrail is about EMPHASIS (lead with money, time, health, fresh air, community, fun) and about preferring 'active transportation' as our own term for what we do. It is not a banned word, and its ordinary sense of 'something you can keep up' is legitimate. seo/strategy.md overstated this as 'never' and was corrected 2026-09-22. This is the SECOND time the routine raised the word as a finding (the first was the MassCEC listing, declined 2026-09-14); there should not be a third.
